description.narrative:
The appeal is necessary due to:
Flooding Impact: The worst floods in decades have devastated homes, agriculture, and infrastructure, displacing thousands. Food Insecurity: 1.37 million people are facing a food security crisis, with 120,923 in emergency conditions. Health Risks: Contaminated water sources and inadequate sanitation have heightened the risks of waterborne and vector-borne diseases. Conflict and Displacement: Armed conflicts and insecurity have exacerbated vulnerabilities, especially for migrants and IDPs. Underfunding: As of September 2024, less than 30% of the required funding for Mali’s Humanitarian Response Plan had been secured.

The appeal targets:
200,000 people from the most vulnerable groups, including women, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities. Priority regions: Bamako, Kayes, Koulikoro, Sikasso, Gao, Ségou, Mopti, and Timbuktu. IDPs, migrants, and communities in high-risk or flood-prone areas.

The emergency appeal addresses the complex humanitarian crisis in Mali, caused by severe flooding, armed conflicts, and mass displacement. The crisis has resulted in:
Over 2 million people affected. 91 deaths, 148 injuries, and the destruction of 40,445 homes. 85,566 hectares of farmland destroyed and 733,683 tons of grain lost, severely impacting food security. 330,713 internally displaced persons (IDPs) as of May 2024, living in overcrowded and inadequate shelters.

The intervention is structured into two main phases:
Immediate Emergency Response (October–December 2024):
Provision of shelter kits, essential household items, and food assistance. Financial assistance for vulnerable households. Distribution of hygiene kits, insecticide-treated mosquito nets, and psychological first aid. Post-Emergency Relief and Recovery (January–October 2025):
Supporting community recovery through cash and in-kind assistance. Climate adaptation initiatives, including training and community resilience programs. Formation of multi-functional National Disaster Response Teams (NDRTs) and preparedness planning.

The operation focuses on the regions of:
Bamako Kayes Koulikoro Sikasso Gao Ségou Mopti Timbuktu These areas are prioritized based on the scale of the impact from flooding, displacement, and food insecurity.
